text:
Epic lodged from docs/plans/2026-07-26-evidence-coherence-representation.md.

Only four blocking edges were encoded, because only four are genuinely forced: P7.2 blocked by P7.3 (dependency decision), P6f.12 blocked by P7.2 (representation before hand-writing every codec), and P7.6 blocked by both (baseline after the API churn). The rest of the sequence is preference, not constraint, and is recorded in the epic body so it does not masquerade as a hard dependency.

P6f.18 is deliberately NOT split into a second bead here; P7.6 carries its release half, and P6f.18 keeps the infrastructure half. Existing beads (P6f.5a, .10, .12, .16, .18, .23, .33a) are related to this epic and gate it, but keep their P6f parentage so the P6f epic's own completion rule stays intact.

Two open questions for the owner, both recorded in the plan: whether scodec-bits is acceptable as a direct kernel/core/protocol dependency (P7.3 decides, and a NO rescopes or drops P7.2), and whether P7.1 is attempted at all given Docker would not start on the review machine.
